title: paulmisc: Epidemiological Visualization & SQL Tools
text: Create simple epidemic curve simulated outbreak data:
code: # Simulate a point-source outbreak cases <- simulate_outbreak(n = 50, seed = 42)  # Create basic epicurve ggplot(cases, aes(x = onset_date)) +   geom_epicurve() +   labs(     title = "Outbreak Epicurve",     x = "Date of Onset",     y = "Number of Cases"   ) +   theme_minimal()

title: paulmisc: Epidemiological Visualization & SQL Tools
text: Visualise cases demographic clinical characteristics:
code: # Colour by age group ggplot(cases, aes(x = onset_date, fill = age_group)) +   geom_epicurve(colour = "grey20") +   scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +   labs(     title = "Cases by Age Group",     x = "Date of Onset",     y = "Number of Cases",     fill = "Age Group"   ) +   theme_bw()

title: paulmisc: Epidemiological Visualization & SQL Tools
text: Compare outbreaks across different settings groups:
code: # Facet by setting and colour by outcome ggplot(cases, aes(x = onset_date, fill = outcome)) +   geom_epicurve(height = 0.85) +   facet_wrap(~ setting, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +   scale_fill_manual(     values = c("Recovered" = "steelblue", "Hospitalised" = "tomato")   ) +   labs(     title = "Outbreak Comparison by Setting",     x = "Date of Onset",     y = "Number of Cases",     fill = "Outcome"   ) +   theme_minimal()

title: paulmisc: Epidemiological Visualization & SQL Tools
text: Simulate outbreaks different epidemiological characteristics:
code: # Short incubation period (e.g., food poisoning) short_incubation <- simulate_outbreak(   n = 100,   exposure = as.Date("2024-08-15"),   meanlog = 0.5,   # ~1.6 day median   sdlog = 0.3,   seed = 123 )  # Long incubation period (e.g., viral hepatitis) long_incubation <- simulate_outbreak(   n = 100,   exposure = as.Date("2024-08-15"),   meanlog = 3,     # ~20 day median   sdlog = 0.5,   seed = 123 )  # Compare side by side library(patchwork)  p1 <- ggplot(short_incubation, aes(x = onset_date)) +   geom_epicurve(fill = "coral") +   labs(title = "Short Incubation", x = NULL, y = "Cases") +   theme_minimal()  p2 <- ggplot(long_incubation, aes(x = onset_date)) +   geom_epicurve(fill = "skyblue") +   labs(title = "Long Incubation", x = "Date of Onset", y = "Cases") +   theme_minimal()  p1 / p2

title: paulmisc: Epidemiological Visualization & SQL Tools
text: Fine-tune appearance individual case squares:
code: # Adjust spacing and size ggplot(cases, aes(x = onset_date, fill = sex)) +   geom_epicurve(     width = 0.8,   # Horizontal spacing (0-1)     height = 0.95, # Vertical spacing (0-1, higher = less gap)     colour = "white",     linewidth = 0.2   ) +   scale_fill_manual(values = c("Male" = "#0072B2", "Female" = "#D55E00")) +   labs(     title = "Cases by Sex with Custom Styling",     x = "Date of Onset",     y = "Number of Cases"   ) +   theme_dark()

title: Epicurve geom: one square per case — geom_epicurve
text: geom_epicurve() draws classical epidemiological curve every individual case rendered small square stacked top others sharing date (binning unit x-axis). companion stat, stat_epicurve(), assigns case vertical stacking position within x-value bin.

title: Epicurve geom: one square per case — geom_epicurve
code: geom_epicurve(   mapping = NULL,   data = NULL,   stat = "epicurve",   position = "identity",   ...,   width = 0.9,   height = 0.9,   na.rm = FALSE,   show.legend = NA,   inherit.aes = TRUE )  stat_epicurve(   mapping = NULL,   data = NULL,   geom = "epicurve",   position = "identity",   ...,   width = 0.9,   na.rm = FALSE,   show.legend = NA,   inherit.aes = TRUE )

title: Epicurve geom: one square per case — geom_epicurve
text: mapping Set aesthetic mappings created ggplot2::aes(). data data displayed layer. stat statistical transformation use data; defaults "epicurve". position Position adjustment, defaults "identity". ... arguments passed ggplot2::layer(). width Numeric width case square x-axis units. daily date data days; defaults 0.9. height Numeric height case square y-axis units; defaults 0.9. Values 1 produce visible gaps stacked cases. na.rm FALSE (default), missing values removed warning. show.legend Logical. layer included legends? inherit.aes FALSE, overrides default aesthetics rather combining . geom geometric object use; defaults "epicurve".

title: Run Redshift SQL Query Builder Shiny App — run_redshift_query_builder
text: Launches interactive Shiny application building Amazon Redshift SQL queries without writing code. app provides intuitive interface form-based inputs constructing complex SQL queries including table selection, column specifications, conditions, date filters, GROUP , ORDER , .

title: Run Redshift SQL Query Builder Shiny App — run_redshift_query_builder
code: run_redshift_query_builder(background = TRUE, ...)

title: Run Redshift SQL Query Builder Shiny App — run_redshift_query_builder
text: background Logical. TRUE (default), runs app background R process (requires callr package), allowing continued use console. FALSE, blocks console app stopped. ... Additional arguments passed shiny::runApp() background = FALSE.

title: Run Redshift SQL Query Builder Shiny App — run_redshift_query_builder
text: background = FALSE, invisibly returns result shiny::runApp(). background = TRUE (default), returns process handle callr::r_bg() can used monitor terminate background process. process returned visibly can easily assign variable.

title: Run Redshift SQL Query Builder Shiny App — run_redshift_query_builder
text: Redshift SQL Query Builder includes: Table Selection: Specify schema, table name, optional alias Column Selection: Choose columns, specific columns, aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, COUNT DISTINCT) Conditions: Add 3 conditions /logic, supporting operators like =, !=, >, <, LIKE, , , NULL, etc. Date Filters: Filter date ranges, last N days, current month/year, specific dates using Redshift functions Sorting & Grouping: GROUP , , ORDER , LIMIT, OFFSET Validation: Real-time error checking helpful messages Copy Clipboard: One-click copy generated SQL

title: Run Redshift SQL Query Builder Shiny App — run_redshift_query_builder
text: app requires shiny bslib packages. Running background mode (default) requires callr package.

title: Run Redshift SQL Query Builder Shiny App — run_redshift_query_builder
code: if (interactive()) {   # Run in background (default) - IMPORTANT: assign to variable   app <- run_redshift_query_builder()      # Continue using console for other work...      # Stop the app when done   app$kill()      # Run in foreground (blocks console)   # run_redshift_query_builder(background = FALSE) }

what: Simulate onset dates for a point-source disease outbreak — simulate_outbreak
title: Simulate onset dates for a point-source disease outbreak — simulate_outbreak
text: Generates small, realistic line list single point-source outbreak. Incubation periods drawn log-normal distribution (classical choice many enteric respiratory pathogens), producing right-skewed onset distribution typical point-source events. handful categorical case attributes (age group, sex, outcome, setting) simulated alongside, resulting data frame can used demonstrate test plotting functions geom_epicurve().

title: Simulate onset dates for a point-source disease outbreak — simulate_outbreak
code: simulate_outbreak(   n = 20,   exposure = as.Date("2024-06-01"),   meanlog = 1.6,   sdlog = 0.45,   seed = 42 )

title: Simulate onset dates for a point-source disease outbreak — simulate_outbreak
text: n Integer. Number cases simulate. Defaults 20. exposure Date (object coercible Date) giving common point-source exposure date. Defaults "2024-06-01". meanlog, sdlog Numeric. Parameters log-normal incubation period distribution log scale, passed stats::rlnorm(). Defaults (meanlog = 1.6, sdlog = 0.45) give median incubation period roughly five days. seed Optional integer used seed random number generator reproducibility. Use NULL leave RNG state untouched.

title: Simulate onset dates for a point-source disease outbreak — simulate_outbreak
text: data frame one row per case columns case_id, onset_date, age_group, sex, outcome, setting.

title: Simulate onset dates for a point-source disease outbreak — simulate_outbreak
code: cases <- simulate_outbreak() head(cases) #>   case_id onset_date age_group    sex      outcome   setting #> 1    C001 2024-06-10     Adult Female    Recovered Wedding B #> 2    C002 2024-06-05     Adult   Male    Recovered Wedding B #> 3    C003 2024-06-07     Adult   Male    Recovered Wedding A #> 4    C004 2024-06-08   Elderly   Male    Recovered Wedding B #> 5    C005 2024-06-07     Adult   Male Hospitalised Wedding A #> 6    C006 2024-06-06   Elderly   Male    Recovered Wedding B  # A larger outbreak with a different exposure date big <- simulate_outbreak(n = 100, exposure = as.Date("2025-03-15")) range(big$onset_date) #> [1] "2025-03-16" "2025-03-29"
